item.title: Bernardo Silva hails Real Madrid dominance as red-hot Blancos extend winning streak with Valencia demolition
item.description: FBL-ESP-LIGA-VALENCIA-REAL MADRID - AFP Bernardo Silva has praised Real Madrid's defensive solidity after a commanding 3-0 victory over Valencia at Mestalla. The Portuguese star believes their eighth consecutive win puts the club in a prime position to challenge for both Liga and Champions League glory this season. Real Madrid secure impressive victory Silva played a starring role as Madrid cruised to a 3-0 victory against Valencia at Mestalla. The Portuguese midfielder featured for 84 minutes during an excellent individual display in the heart of the pitch. The impressive away result marked an eighth consecutive win across all competitions for the Spanish club. Jose Mourinho’s side currently sits in second place in the Liga standings with 30 points - level with league leaders Barcelona, ​​who are set to play their 12th match of the campaign against Atletico Madrid. Silva highlights aggressive Valencia approach The match was not without its challenges for the visiting side. Silva noted the physical nature of their opponents and the lenient officiating that allowed the game to flow freely. "A tough match, in a challenging atmosphere, against an aggressive team and a referee who allowed them to be aggressive," Silva explained on the club's official website . "That made it complicated for us. Fede's [Valverde] stunning goal helped us control the game. I felt we always had control of the match and were very organized, managing their transitions very well. The defenders were very aggressive and won quick balls. We're very happy to secure three more points. "Having eight consecutive wins puts us in a much better position to fight for La Liga and be among the top eight in the Champions League. We're very happy with this streak, but now we need to focus on the next match and keep going because the atmosphere in the dressing room and at the club is very good. We want to keep winning and winning." Maintaining the winning streak Los Blancos have now recorded eight consecutive victories across all competitions. The last time they failed to secure a win was during the Madrid Derby against Atletico in late September. Silva emphasized that this achievement is crucial for his team if they wish to remain in contention for the title this season. "It's very important because the teams that defend best are always ready to win matches and titles," he added. "That puts us closer to winning games and championships." International duty calls for Silva Club football now pauses for the international break. Silva will immediately shift his focus to international duty and travel to join his Portugal team-mates. Portugal are preparing for two important UEFA Nations League fixtures in the coming days. They will face Denmark on November 14 before concluding the international window against Wales on November 17.

item.title: Bayern Munich not taking any guff from 1860 honks
item.description: (Photo by Leonhard Simon/Getty Images) | Getty Images The rivalry between Bayern Munich and 1860 Munich is never particularly short on hostility, but one incident during Bayern’s Bundesliga title celebrations at Marienplatz has now developed into a legal dispute that is showing no signs of slowing down. On May 17, as Bayern Munich celebrated another league title in front of thousands of supporters and live television cameras, supporters of local rivals 1860 Munich managed to smuggle an insulting banner into the event and unfurl it in the fan se ction. Bayern subsequently filed a criminal complaint against persons unknown for insult, with the club taking issue not only with the message but also with the use and defacement of its logo. The matter has now reached the home of one alleged participant. According to Bild , poli ce recently searched the apartment of a suspect believed to have been involved in the incident. Four detectives from the Munich Criminal Investigation Department carried out the search under an emergency warrant issued by the Munich District Court. Computers and other electronic devices were seized as investigator s looked for potential evidence, including receipts, bank transfers, and chat logs. Interestingly, Bild (via @iMiaSanMia ) re ports that the suspect’s lawyer described the officers as very friendly, claiming they even chuckled at the prank. That detail has not exactly helped make the investigation look less unusual from the defense’s perspective. Sebastian Wagner, a defense attorney who regularly represents 1860 Munich supporters in criminal proceedings, strongly disputes the legal basis for the case: “The behavior described doe s not constitute a criminal offense. FC Bayern AG is also not a collective entity that can be the victim of an insult.” Wagner is also unhappy that aut horities carried out a search in the first place, suggesting that Bayern’s influence may have played a role in the judiciary’s response: “You get the impression that FC Bayern says, ‘Jump,’ and the Munich judicia ry asks, ‘How high?’” Bayern Munich, however, has its own explanation for pursuing the matter. The club reportedly had two prim ary objectives. First, it wanted the derogatory banner handed over so that its logo would no longer remain in circulation in that form. Second, Bayern ultimately decided to take legal action because it does not tolerate its logo being defaced or disparaged, particularly out of a se nse of responsibility toward its supporters. And the accused supporter is apparently not interested in backing down. Speaking through his lawyer, the 1860 Munich fan delivered a response that sounds very much in keeping with the rivalry: “A derby lasts 90 minutes. But in court, I would also take on FC Bayern all the way into stoppage time.” Well, there is certainly no shortage of confidence on either side. What began as a rival supporters’ attempt to hijack Bayern Munich’s title celebration has becom e a rather unusual legal showdown

item.title: Relative calmness among top bosses between Barcelona and Atletico Madrid ahead of La Liga clash
item.description: Relative calmness among top bosses between Barcelona and Atletico Madrid ahead of La Liga clash La Liga will witness one of the its most consequential matches this weekend, in the context of the title race, as Barcelona travel to Metropolitano to face Atletico Madrid this evening. The two sides are coming on the back of a controversial summer, where Barcelona tried hard to prize away Atleti’s star player Julian Alvarez, leading to an intense war of word between both club bosses. As Barcelona visit the Metropolitano, one would expect animosity from fans and in the stands. But as far as the leadership is concerned, it appears things have softened a bit. Relative calm among leadership Laporta will lead the Barcelona delegation. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) According to Mundo Deportivo , there will be a notable easing of tension among the leaders of both Barcelona and Atletico Madrid, in the VIP box, following recent appeals for peace from the leaders of both clubs. President Joan Laporta, who will lead the Barcelona delegation in Madrid, revealed last month at the European Football Clubs Assembly in Copenhagen that he had “smoothed things over” with Atletico CEO Miguel Angel Gil Marin. Atletico president Enrique Cerezo has similarly adopted a similar tone, though he did not hold back when asked about Alvarez ahead of this game. That thaw between the two set of leaders will be reflected in the first lunch meeting between the two boards since the Alvarez saga in the summer. Cerezo, alongside club legend and board member David Villa, are expected to host Laporta and the Barcelona delegation, also including vice-presidents Rafa Yuste, Elena Fort and Ferran Olive. The report adds that Deco, Bojan Krkic and Alejandro Echevarria will be present in the VIP box but absent from the lunch, while Gil Marin is expected to skip it to focus on the match itself. Fire in the stands Atleti fans are expected to be hostile towards Barcelona after Alvarez saga. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) Although it seems the mood in the boardroom has mellowed, the atmosphere inside the stadium will be quite different, the report says. Indeed, the home fans are eager to welcome Barcelona with intensity of a big European night. They are expected to be greeted by flares and hostility in what will be a full house at the Metropolitano. The anger will not be aimed at Alvarez but the Barcelona team, which is hardly surprising as the relationship between the two clubs was at a breaking point in the summer.

item.description: Perfect moment came and went but Leeds United show full personality - Graham Smyth's Verdict The perfect moment appeared to have escaped Leeds United but the perfect result could not. Sometimes you don't get what you deserve in football and having been various shades of unfortunate in recent weeks, Leeds' job against Tottenham Hotspur was simply to win by any means. A scruffy victory from an own goal would have done it for almost everyone of a Leeds persuasion - particularly going into an international break having waited for victory since mid-September. But an intoxicating second half offering of sheer bloody-mindedness and good football was too good for the footballing Gods to ignore. Not that there was anything handed to the Whites. They fought for everything they held in their hands when the full-time whistle went on a 1-0 win. Victory hinged entirely on what happened after the break, because the first half was not a memorable one, barring a pair of VAR checks. Sean Longstaff, starting his 200th Premier League game, was one of a number of white shirts to stick to Mateus Fernandes every time Spurs tried to play out in the opening moments. Forcing the visitors to go long played into Leeds' strength and in turn earned them possession with which to attack early on. On the ball Gabriel Gudmundsson enjoyed a lot of time on the ball and opportunities to cross. It was his pressure that led to the game's first flashpoint and a possible VAR intervention. Fernandes fell towards the ball with his arm outstretched and while one angle made it seem like he must have handled it, another showed the contact was somewhere between shoulder and sleeve. Ao Tanaka and Ethan Ampadu both sent early efforts wide, the latter's effort more wayward than his midfield partner's, and there were numerous crosses into the Spurs box that gave Dominic Calvert-Lewin little chance of causing problems. James Justin's from the right was the best of the lot and even that was well dealt with. The rest of the half was a scrappy, niggly affair. item.title: “A massive honour”: Man United Women star Ella Toone beams after collecting yet another award
item.description: “A massive honour”: Man United Women star Ella Toone beams after collecting yet another award Manchester United Women star Ella Toone has been rewarded with a prize in recognition of her contribution to football. United career Toone began her career with United in 2018 when the club was reformed and started out in the second division. She has won the Championship and also an FA Cup title. Toone is the club’s record appearance maker with 222 appearances and is also the club’s record goalscorer with 66 strikes in all competitions. The attacker has also achieved success with England , winning both Euro 2022 and 2025. She also had the joy of scoring in the final at Wembley in 2022. The award The club’s official site reported, “in a celebration of Manchester and its culture, this week’s This Is Manchester Awards recognised Ella’s incredible contribution to the game at its annual awards ceremony.” Toone’s contribution to the game extends well beyond the pitch, as she also set up the ET7 Academy last year, which is a “football development initiative through which she aims to provide an environment for young girls between the ages of eight and 19 to learn the game, develop, and aspire to fulfil their own footballing dreams.” What’s more, she also took up a role as a creative and strategic advisor to Chorley Women Football Club this summer. Commenting on her award to MUTV after the event, she claimed, “it’s a massive honour, it’s nice to win these awards. All I want to do is perform on the pitch, be a role model, and use my platform as much as I can to inspire young girls and boys.” She continued, “it’s so nice to be able to be in this position where I can really use my platform in a positive way, help young girls and boys start out in their journeys and give equal opportunities to everyone. It’s something I’m really, really proud of and that I enjoy doing.” Toone will next be in action for United Women later this afternoon when they travel to Aston Villa in the WSL. item.title: Joe Hart hails Celtic’s ‘absolute saviour’ after dramatic Europa League victory
item.description: Joe Hart hails Celtic’s ‘absolute saviour’ after dramatic Europa League victory Former Celtic goalkeeper Joe Hart has hailed Camilo Durán as an “absolute saviour” for Martin O’Neill’s side this season, while praising Callum Osmand’s ability to produce moments of magic. The Englishman was delighted to see his former club secure their first Europa League victory of the campaign with a dramatic 3-2 comeback win over Besiktas on Thursday night. Despite Celtic’s inconsistent performances domestically, Hart believes their results are comparable to previous title-winning campaigns, insisting the biggest concern has been the lack of fluency in their attacking play. Speaking on The Overlap Daily, Hart said: “That’s the thing about that club, and that is why I adore it, and I’m so pleased that I got to spend time there and be a part of it. The expectancy and the expectation, unless you are a Celtic man or a Celtic person, you wouldn’t understand, because, like you say, they’re still top. “I think Rangers have a game in hand because they played in a cup semi-final at the weekend, but even if they win that, they’re still a point behind. And domestically, Celtic have lost two and drawn one in 11 games. It’s not the reason. I was looking at how they’ve started leagues in the past eight, nine years, and they’re right up there with what they do, but they’re not flowing. The strikers aren’t scoring. “Camilo Durán has been an absolute saviour this season. Him and Callum Osmand came on, I think, around the 60th minute, with it looking ominous, 1-0 down against Besiktas, who were flying high, a good team. “And Callum Osmand’s first touch, he smashed it through bodies. He’s got that magic moment in him. He had it last year. He’s the one who scored when they beat Heart of Midlothian 3-1, and he got to run the length of the field on his own. He scored a couple of big goals in the title run-in as well. “But it made me happy to feel the stadium shake through the TV, because that stadium does go wild, and people are talking with their feet. item.title: 'I can't believe he is one of us' - inside Salah's life in Trabzon
item.description: Mohamed Salah has scored 10 goals in 15 games for Turkish club Trabzonspor [Getty Images] Back in August, when Mohamed Salah landed in Istanbul after flying in from his holiday in Mykonos, he wore Trabzonspor's burgundy and blue home strip as he stepped out of the plane to be greeted by thousands of fans. That kit sold out almost instantly. Later that day, as Salah headed to Trabzon in north-east Turkey to complete the formalities of one of the most unexpected transfers, he asked one of his entourage what he should wear. "The same kit," came the response, but Trabzonspor president Ertugrul Dogan advised Salah to wear the black away kit instead. Of course, that sold out too. From the outset of the 34-year-old's arrival to this historic port city on the Black Sea, that sense of adulation has only grown. "I went to the airport to see him in Istanbul and it was surreal," says Nisa Dumangoz. "I still can't believe that he is one of us." Go for a stroll through Trabzon on matchday and it is Salah's face which adorns everything. Even the walls inside the fishmongers have pictures of him. At the club shop in town, one of the staff jokes that the ground floor is for the Egyptian and the upper floor is for everything else. Outside the stadium, there are scarves, magnets, keyrings, lighters with his face on and Egyptian Nemes headdresses in Trabzonspor colours. Season ticket sales rocketed after his arrival. "Walking around Trabzon, it feels as though nine out of every 10 fans wearing a shirt have Salah's name on the back. The 10th has their own," says Turkish football journalist Hasan Tuncel. The club have surpassed their merchandise revenue from last year in three months since Salah's arrival, while the local airport is only getting busier. Liverpool was difficult to reach for many supporters across the Arab world and tickets were often hard to source. Trabzon is far more accessible, with new flights introduced from Cairo, Dubai and Riyadh since Salah's arrival. On our flight from Istanbul, we meet an Egyptian family of 10 coming from Cairo for Trabzonspor's Uefa Conference League game against Freiburg. "He is our ambassador and our Egyptian King, and with how many people want to come to Turkey now, he is their ambassador too," says Mahmoud. At the game, there is a group of Egyptian celebrities and influencers. A quick check of their social media shows their combined Instagram following of about five million. Trabzonspor have three million. Salah has 68 million. Salah recently went for a hike and posed for a picture on a rock in the Trabzon highlands. That rock has been renamed Salahtasi (Salah's Rock) and is now a tourist destination. The commercial element of his signing has more than been justified but crucially, on the pitch, Salah is driving Trabzonspor's push for the Turkish Super Lig title and he has hit the ground running with 10 goals and five assists in all competitions. item.title: Report: Liverpool will look to exploit a major weakness in Crystal Palace
item.description: Report: Liverpool will look to exploit a major weakness in Crystal Palace Crystal Palace v Liverpool: Away Form Meets Palace Pressure at Selhurst Park Crystal Palace arrive at this game in a state of anxiety, Liverpool arrive carrying irritation, and somewhere in that collision sits the shape of a compelling Premier League afternoon. According to BBC Football , this is a meeting between a home side sinking under the weight of grim numbers and an away side trying to prove that one bad week does not become a damaging trend. Palace’s predicament is stark. Pierre Sage has watched his team slide into the bottom three after a run that has stripped confidence and exposed weakness after weakness. The defeat to Tottenham offered a brutal snapshot of where they are. Jean-Philippe Mateta’s early dismissal wrecked the script, but what followed went beyond misfortune. Palace were overwhelmed in every department, pinned back, starved of possession and barely able to cross the halfway line with any purpose. Those figures matter because they fit a wider pattern. Palace have been conceding heavily, losing regularly and producing the kind of statistical profile that usually sends clubs towards relegation trouble. They have allowed far more shots than they have created themselves, and that imbalance is often a merciless judge over the long haul. When a team spends that much time defending, errors multiply, belief ebbs away and every opponent begins to sense vulnerability. Crystal Palace Struggles Laid Bare The most troubling part for Sage may be that the flaws are not subtle. Palace have become particularly susceptible in the air, with headed goals against them already mounting at an alarming rate. Defensive issues can often be dressed up as bad luck for a while, but repeated punishment from the same source points to a structural problem. Organisation, aggression and concentration all come into question. Yet football seldom respects neat scripts. Palace can still draw on a recent record against Liverpool that offers some encouragement. This fixture has become less one-sided than it once was, and Selhurst Park has provided them with resistance and reward in recent meetings. That does not erase current form, but it does suggest Liverpool will not be handed anything. Liverpool Away Form Offers Encouragement Liverpool, for their part, have reason to feel aggrieved by how the past few days have unfolded. Andoni Iraola began his reign with poise and momentum, yet successive defeats have checked the early glow. The loss to Fenerbahce was especially frustrating because of the manner of the goals conceded, all from set-pieces, and because it raised uncomfortable questions about control and concentration at key moments. IMAGO Iraola described those concessions as “cheap” and “messy”. He was equally agitated by the home defeat to Arsenal, a game in which Liverpool were not outclassed but still ended up making unwanted history by failing to register a shot on target at Anfield

item.title: Report: Spurs to make formal complaint after Leeds United defeat
item.description: Report: Spurs to make formal complaint after Leeds United defeat Tottenham to Lodge Formal Complaint After Mathys Tel Injury in Leeds Defeat Tottenham are preparing to make a formal complaint to Pro Ref after Jayden Bogle avoided a red card for the challenge that forced Mathys Tel off in the 1-0 loss to Leeds United. According to Standard , Spurs want clarity on why no dismissal followed despite a four-minute VAR review at Elland Road. The incident has quickly become the central talking point from a damaging afternoon for Roberto De Zerbi’s side. Bogle landed studs-up on Tel’s left Achilles, with the Tottenham forward attempting to continue before signalling that he could not carry on. He was later seen on crutches and in a protective boot, heightening concern over the severity of the problem. Mathys Tel injury concern grows There is now real anxiety inside Tottenham over the extent of the Mathys Tel injury. De Zerbi indicated after the match that further checks would follow, but the early outlook was troubling. The expectation is that the Frenchman could face a significant spell out, which would represent a major setback given his growing importance in the attack. Spurs also appear to feel the match turned at that point. Tel’s withdrawal disrupted their shape and threat, and Leeds gradually seized momentum before Noah Okafor scored the winner in the 79th minute. VAR decision leaves Spurs seeking answers The key issue for Tottenham is the process around the VAR decision. Bogle escaped any punishment, and Spurs now want an explanation from the officiating body as to how that conclusion was reached. In a game defined by fine margins, the sense at the club is that a serious challenge went insufficiently addressed. Photo IMAGO De Zerbi struck a measured tone afterwards, even after his own frustration on the touchline brought a yellow card and a touchline ban for the upcoming home match against Ipswich. He said, “No, I have big confidence in the referee.” He added, “Nothing changes if he goes to watch the clip or not. I think there was the VAR, and if they didn’t take the right decision, I don’t know. But we have confidence, we have to keep our eyes on the performance where we can improve.” Our View This is exactly the sort of episode that leaves people furious. A player ends up leaving on crutches and in a protective boot, there is a lengthy VAR review, and somehow nobody decides the challenge warrants even the strongest sanction available. It is very hard to square that with any claim of consistency. item.description: Lionel Messi makes MLS history with back-to-back Golden Boot wins despite Decision Day blank Lionel Messi has won the MLS Golden Boot for a second consecutive season, becoming the the first player in the league's history to win the award back to back. The Inter Miami captain ended the 2026 regular season on 26 goals, four clear of FC Dallas striker Petar Musa on 22. Nashville SC's Sam Surridge finished third with 21 goals, with Vancouver Whitecaps forward Brian White one further back. The crown arrived on a frustrating final day. Messi failed to score as Miami let a 3-0 home lead slip against Charlotte FC, settling for a 3-3 draw. Lionel Messi's numbers behind a second Golden Boot This year's tally fell short of the 29 goals Messi scored in 2025, which was the fourth-highest total ever recorded in a single MLS season. Carlos Vela holds the all-time record with 34 regular-season goals for Los Angeles FC in 2019. Messi's creative output also remained elite. He provided 17 assists, one fewer than league leader Pep Biel. The individual highlight of his campaign came in August, when he scored four times in a 7-1 rout of Montreal. Inter Miami turn to the MLS Cup defence Inter Miami now begin their bid to retain the MLS Cup, a feat no club has achieved since LA Galaxy in 2011/12. As the Eastern Conference's No. 2 seed, behind record-setting Nashville, they meet No. 7 Columbus Crew in a best-of-three first round. Messi is also chasing a third straight MLS MVP award. Before his repeat win last season, no player had ever won it in consecutive years, and Predrag Radosavljević (1997, 2003) was the only previous two-time winner. The award is voted on by media, players and club staff.

item.title: Arteta hails 'different' Noni Madueke as Arsenal winger responds to England snubs
item.description: Arteta hails 'different' Noni Madueke as Arsenal winger responds to England snubs Mikel Arteta believes Noni Madueke has returned as a 'different' player since deciding to train on his own during the last international break, and the Arsenal manager has now challenged the winger to go again. Madueke was Arsenal's main attacking outlet in Saturday's 1-0 win over Hull City. His stinging shot forced a save from Konstantinos Tzolakis, and Martin Odegaard followed up to score the only goal of the game. His 13 touches in the opposition box were the most by an Arsenal player in any Premier League game this season. Involved heavily throughout, no player had more dribbles (5) or more chances created and shots combined (8). Yet the 24-year-old left the pitch frustrated. Late on, Mikel Merino slipped him through, but his attempt to round Tzolakis clipped the goalkeeper's foot and the chance was gone. "He knew he had three clear chances to score," Arteta said. Noni Madueke's response to being left out Madueke started only two of Arsenal's first seven games this season and was not picked by Thomas Tuchel for England for last month's Nations League fixtures. Rather than sulk, Arteta revealed that he used the international break to train individually. The change since has been stark. He did not complete a full Premier League match last season, his first after joining from Chelsea in the summer of 2025. Since the break, he has played the full 90 minutes in four of Arsenal's five league games, and came off the bench at half-time in the other to curl in the winner against Nottingham Forest. He scored the opener in the Champions League in midweek against Slavia Prague, and Bukayo Saka's injury against Bayern Munich has moved him back to the right, where he is now central to Arteta's plans. However, despite that improved form and Saka's absence, he was again overlooked by England for the upcoming break. “It was a close call and a difficult decision not to bring Noni, because he got his minutes after Bukayo’s injury at Arsenal,” Tuchel said at a post-squad selection press conference at Wembley. “He got some goals. It was very close. But also [in that position], we stuck with the group that we had [during the last international break] and give them our trust.” Arteta made clear Madueke had to earn his chance. "But that's the second part of the story," he told reporters. "The first one is you need to earn the right to be able to do that. Noni did. He didn't do it in the first part of the season; that's why he wasn't playing. "But the way he reacted to that is a great example for the rest of the squad, which is: I want to do more. He went away, decided to train, came back, and he was a different Noni. You could sense that he meant business, and he wasn't going to accept that situation. Since then, he's been incredible. So now you are in that position, now you need to hold it and improve it, and he can still do that. So, let's see what he does in this break."

We've had Katie Taylor against Amanda Serrano and Claressa Shields against Savannah Marshall. Those were massive occasions that took women's boxing to another level. item.description: ISTANBUL, TURKEY - NOVEMBER 04: Head coach Andoni Iraola of Liverpool FC looks on during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD4 match between Fenerbahce SK and Liverpool FC at Fenerbahce Sükrü Saracoglu Spor Kompleksi on November 04, 2026 in Istanbul, Turkey. (Photo by Ferda Demir/Getty Images) | Getty Images This time last week, Liverpool fans were looking at the upcoming fixtures as a means to measure how far Andoni Iraola’s Reds have come in terms of implementing their project. Now, with two losses on the trot, fans are hoping that they can arrest the mini-slide before the international break. Last week, Liverpool managed back-to-back losses for the first time in what feels like forever. First, Liverpool put up a rather decent fight against the reigning Premier League Champions, putting together a higher xG before eventually losing to the Gunners 1-nil. It’s the kind of result that, if taken in isolation, one could argue shows that Liverpool are trending in the right direction: they tested the champs and looked decent. It’s not, say, as good a performance as pre-red card Manchester City, but it was more than capable. Which is really a big deal. Iraola’s task seemed big given how disjointed this club has looked for most of 2026. And even if you believed, as I do, that this club has far too much talent for results not to come eventually, it’s still certainly been great to experience a version of Liverpool that doesn’t make you worried that they’d be completely outworked and out thought even before the first kick. In many ways, it’s just great to watch a competent Liverpool. item.title: Inter Miami star Lionel Messi makes MLS history with incredible back-to-back Golden Boot awards
item.description: Atlanta United FC v Inter Miami CF - Getty Images Sport Lionel Messi has cemented his legacy in the United States by becoming the first player to win back-to-back MLS Golden Boot awards. The Inter Miami forward finished the 2026 Major League Soccer regular season with 26 goals, proving he remains in a class of his own at 39 years old. Messi secures historic consecutive Golden Boot awards Messi has rewritten the history books by becoming the first player to win back-to-back MLS Golden Boot awards. The Inter Miami forward finished the 2026 Major League Soccer regular season with a league-high 26 goals to his name. The 39-year-old achieved this remarkable scoring feat across 31 appearances, which included 29 starts for his club. He ultimately finished four goals clear of his nearest challenger, FC Dallas forward Petar Musa, while Nashville SC striker Sam Surridge took third place with 21 goals. Messi is now just the sixth player to finish with the most goals in multiple MLS regular seasons. His prolific form also included 17 assists, giving him an astonishing league-high 43 goal contributions overall. Inter Miami coach backs Messi for MVP The legendary forward previously won the Golden Boot in 2025 after scoring 29 goals in just 28 regular-season matches. Having already claimed the prestigious MVP award in 2024 and 2025, he remains the heavy favourite to win the trophy again in 2026. If successful, the recently retired Argentina international will become the first three-time MVP winner in MLS history. Inter Miami head coach Kily Gonzalez firmly believes his star player is fully deserving of the historic accolade. "I have no doubt that he's the best of all," Gonzalez said,as quoted by ESPN . "None of them can compare to him when it comes to respect for his colleagues. Leo at his age and what he does, from my point of view, deserves the MVP and also the Ballon d'Or," Gonzalez added. "I hope he can achieve it." A dramatic end to the regular season Messi failed to score in Inter Miami's final game of the regular season, but he was heavily involved as they drew 3-3 with Charlotte FC . He provided the corner that led to Ian Fray's early opener and later contributed to Luis Suarez's close-range strike. Inter Miami inexplicably surrendered a commanding 3-0 half-time lead in that match, ultimately finishing second in the Eastern Conference with 60 points. Nashville SC topped the table with 77 points, breaking Miami's previous single-season record from 2024. Inter Miami prepare for a playoff push Despite missing out on the top spot, the Herons have safely clinched a playoff berth following another strong domestic campaign. Their final league position also secured a ticket to the upcoming Concacaf Champions Cup for a fourth consecutive time. Messi and his team-mates must now regroup quickly ahead of a crucial post-season campaign. They are scheduled to face the seventh-seeded Columbus Crew in a highly anticipated best-of-three first-round playoff series.

(AP Photo/Rick Scuteri) (Rick Scuteri/AP Photo/Rick Scuteri) PHOENIX - Entering Saturday's game, Houston Rockets coach Ime Udoka said the team's keys to victory were limiting the Phoenix Suns' scorers, taking care of the ball and playing at a higher pace. The Rockets failed all those goals for the first 17 minutes of their 102-95 loss at Mortgage Matchup Center, their first two-game losing streak in the young season. In that time, Houston (7-3) let former Rockets Jalen Green make his first four shot attempts, committed eight turnovers leading to 15 Suns (3-5) points and scored zero fastbreak points The issues compounded on each other: Houston couldn't get stops in part because of the turnovers, having to take the ball out of the basket limited the Rockets to operate in the halfcourt against a set defense and that led to long, stagnant, late-clock possessions that often ended in turnovers. "Their physicality at the start, we didn't handle it well again. … Anytime a team that's struggling, you come out and let them be the aggressor, give them confidence and score a 35-point quarter … just make it a dogfight all game," Udoka said. "Got to come out more prepared at the start. We got to have a better start than that." Houston trailed by 18 points before the change, as it often does, came on defense. The Rockets forced turnovers on their own and got some needed WD-40 for their offense. They surged back, winning the second quarter by 12 points to enter halftime tied. A lot of that run came behind a small-ball unit of Fred VanVleet, Amen Thompson, Kevin Durant, Jabari Smith Jr. and Tari Eason that outscored Phoenix by 13 points in about six minutes, per FadeAway. item.title: ‘Luka (Dončić) Overreacted,’ ‘Refund This Man His Money, Adam Silver’ — NBA Fans Rally Behind Ejected Kings Fan After Wife Shares His Side of the Story
item.description: NBA fans defend an ejected Kings spectator after his wife explains the courtside exchange that drew a reaction from Luka Dončić. Kellie DeMarco spoke up for her husband on Saturday, three days after he was ejected from the Los Angeles Lakers’ 116-103 win over the Sacramento Kings at Golden 1 Center. Until then, he had been the courtside spectator in a widely shared clip from Wednesday’s game in which his hard return pass to an official drew a reaction from Luka Dončić. After DeMarco explained what happened from her husband’s perspective, fans quickly weighed in. NBA Fans Back Ejected Kings Spectator After Wife Explains What Happened The sequence began with 2:36 remaining in the third quarter, with the Lakers leading 83-69. After Jarred Vanderbilt blocked a Malik Monk floater out of bounds, the ball landed with the man seated courtside, who sent a hard chest pass back to the baseline official. The Lakers star turned and gestured toward him before security escorted the spectator away. The former TV journalist wrote on Instagram , in part, “Yes, this is my sweet husband, and yes, he’s the guy who got ejected from an NBA game. I spent nearly 20 years in TV news, and he’s getting more airtime than me!” As for the pass, she added, “He played basketball for years, and apparently the chest pass muscle memory never left. He meant no harm, he feels terrible that it came across the wrong way, and he has nothing but respect for the officials.” She also thanked those who reached out, writing, “Thank you for all the kind messages. We love the Kings and this community.” The response largely sided with the couple. “This couple handled everything with pure grace. The ref and Luka should be ashamed,” one fan posted . Another questioned the decision to remove him: “This was the softest ejection of all time. Imagine a chest pass from a fan to a ref half his age warranting an ejection.” The six-time All-Star also drew criticism. “Luka over reacted…. And the internet is nuts,” a fan commented . The Slovenian guard addressed the exchange after Wednesday’s game. “He just tossed it really strong – the ball – toward the ref. I just asked him what the hell he’s doing,” Dončić said . Others argued that the spectator deserved something in return after losing his courtside seat with more than a quarter of the game left. “This guy deserves an apology,” one fan tweeted . “Yeah, you could tell immediately he didn’t mean any harm by it and was genuinely confused. He left without a fight. I hope he gets some kind of compensation,” another added . A third fan wrote , “Refund this man his money, Adam Silver…” The NBA’s Fan Code of Conduct lists fighting, throwing objects, and attempting to enter the court among actions that can lead to immediate ejection. Possible penalties can also include removal without a refund, loss of season tickets, or bans from future games.
